summary: Phase C: log cleanup + orphaned auth removal PASS end-to-end. Backend contract tests reveal a critical bug in POST /api/auth/merge — both keep='email' and keep='wallet' branches crash with MongoDB DuplicateKeyError (unique indexes on users.wallet_address and users.email) because the discarded row still holds the fields being copied to the primary. 5/7 backend tests pass. Frontend UnifiedWalletButton + AccountMergeModal load cleanly with zero console errors and email address renders in the dropdown.

critical.issue: Returns 500 Internal Server Error. Traceback: DuplicateKeyError E11000 on test_database.users index wallet_address_1. email_auth.py:422 writes discarded_row.wallet_address onto primary user row, but the discarded (wallet) user row STILL owns that wallet_address under a unique index → duplicate key crash. Rows ARE moved (archive_unlocks update runs first), but the users row update never lands and the response is 500 so the client sees a failure even though partial state was mutated. Fix: unset wallet_address on the discarded row (or the primary email row) BEFORE writing the new value on primary, or use a single atomic swap.

Returns 500 Internal Server Error. Traceback: DuplicateKeyError E11000 on test_database.users index email_1. email_auth.py:431 writes email/email_verified onto primary (wallet) row, while the discarded (email) row still holds that email under a unique index. Same class of bug as keep='email' branch. Fix: unset email/email_verified on the discarded row before writing to primary. Same partial-mutation problem as above.

action_items: Fix /api/auth/merge duplicate-key bug: before setting wallet_address/email on the primary user row, $unset those fields on the discarded row (or reorder writes so the primary swap is atomic). Applies to both keep='email' and keep='wallet' branches (email_auth.py lines 421-439).

Consider wrapping the merge across identity_collections + users updates in a single transaction so a mid-flight crash doesn't leave archive rows moved but the users row un-linked (currently rows ARE moved before the crashing users.update_one, so a retry after the fix will find the wallet-user row empty of children — this is idempotent-safe but should be documented).

Merge endpoint has NO idempotency check — a second call with the same keep+wallet_user_id will re-run all writes and may set stale wallet/email fields. Consider short-circuiting if discarded_row.merged_into already exists.
critical_code_review_comments: email_auth.py: merge_accounts writes users rows without clearing conflicting unique-indexed fields on the discarded row → guaranteed DuplicateKeyError on any DB with the existing indexes. Bug reproduces 100%.

email_auth.py:339-349: nonce lookup on admin_auth_nonces uses body.message string equality — fine, but relies on exact whitespace. Kept it consistent with admin_auth._build_message so verified working.

AccountMergeModal.jsx: nice UX (recommends 'keep email'); axios call uses `authHeaders` from AuthContext — verified good. No error surfaced from the 500 today (client currently shows detail 'could not merge accounts. try again shortly.'), so the user gets a generic error instead of the underlying duplicate-key which is fine for prod.

success_rate.backend: 71% (5/7 tests pass; 2 fail due to real bug)

Frontend has no known issues — merge modal compiles and renders. Verification of log cleanup: (a) `grep '\[daily-drop\]' frontend console` on fresh /archive visit → 0 hits (verified); (b) `grep daily_drop.request /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log` after triggering a fresh drop → 0 new hits (historical hits from iteration 118 still present in log tail).
rca of the issue: POST /api/auth/merge duplicate-key: Mongo users collection has unique indexes on wallet_address and email. When keep='email', endpoint copies wallet_address from discarded (wallet) row → primary (email) row, but never clears it on the discarded row first — Mongo rejects with E11000 on wallet_address_1. Symmetric bug on keep='wallet' with the email_1 index. Repro: seed a wallet-only user (users.wallet_address=W), sign in as email user E, POST /auth/merge {keep:'email', wallet_user_id:'wallet_'+W} → 500. Mitigation: prepend `await db.users.update_one({user_id:discard_uid},{'$unset':{'wallet_address':1}})` before the primary-row wallet_address update (and symmetrically $unset email/email_verified for the keep='wallet' branch).
